chapter: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
title: Gus Wilson, the self-doubting arranger who walked out
summary: Teddy Wilson's brother Gus wrote beautiful arrangements and tore them up whenever praised, then left his trombone on the chair after a quarrel with Stuff and was never seen again.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Gus could blow a beautiful horn and write beautiful arrangements, but --

It was something -- something with Gus, because see what Gus would do, he would make a nice arrangement, sit up all night, you know, and we'd be talking, and he'd sit up all night making arrangements, you know, and he'd bring it in and pass it out and we'd run it down, you know, play it, and we'd say, "Wow, that sure is great, man." And he'd say, "Oh, don't do me like that, you know. Don't bring me down like that. Don't put me on." He thought we was putting him on. "No, this is beautiful. It's great." And you'd say let's play it again, and we'd play it again, and we'd say, "It's beautiful." And he'd say, "Pass it in. I want to change the introduction," and you'd pass it in and he'd tear it up. So it got so around there for awhile, when he'd arrange we wouldn't say nothing. We'd be quiet as a mouse, because it would be great, you know?

And then one night him and Stuff got to arguing over something small. I forget what it was now. Something that didn't mean nothing, you know. Don't be late next time. You know, or come on the stand. When you see me up here

be up here, you know. Something like that, you know. And he walked out, left his trombone in the chair and walked out, never seen him again. Never seen him again. I run into some band once, and they told me that they saw him on his way to Boston, hitchhiking, with his bag, you know. Sometimes I'll ask Teddy. When I saw Teddy, I'd ask him, and he'd say, "I dont' know where he's at." Because Teddy had him here doing something. I think he wrote a couple of things with Benny Goodman.
